text:
alex: Quick sync — prelaunch checklist for the Growth webinar landing. Need SEO tech pass + redirect safety before we flip paid. Main concern: behavioral redirects (country/variant) might be skewing organic benchmark numbers.

jess: Yep. We saw weird drops in organic sessions during the last test. Are you proposing to disable JS redirects for bots/crawlers? :thinking_face: 

sam: Short answer: yes for crawlers. Also we should add explicit canonical + sitemap priority for the webinar page. That will help SERP stability during the campaign.

alex: Exact asks for eng: 1) Add `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` on experimental variants until go-live. 2) For GA/UTM routing we should avoid client-side 302s that rewrite path — prefer server 302 with `Vary` header or server-side rewrite. 3) Add a temporary redirect suppression flag we can toggle.

marco: Can we do a quick nginx snippet? I can ship a safe toggle. Example I used before:
```
# only set when env WEBINAR_SAFE_REDIRECT=1
if ($http_user_agent ~* "Googlebot|Bingbot|Slurp") {
  add_header X-Robots-Tag "index, follow";
} else {
  return 302 /variant/$arg_variant;
}
```

jess: That looks fine. Two SEO checks I want: meta schema for the webinar event (Event structured data), and ensure internal linking from Resources hub -> landing uses keyword-rich anchor text.

sam: On schema: use `Event` schema with `startDate`, `endDate`, `location` (virtual), and `offers` empty if free. Also add `speakable` snippet for the short description. I'll drop the JSON-LD in the PR.

alex: Also important: redirects map. We have legacy /webinar-old and campaign utm variants. Create a redirect whitelist and a mapping doc so that organic backlinks don't get orphaned. I can ping Partnerships for top referrers list.

seo-bot: crawl-alert: detected 3 incoming links to /webinar-old from high-authority domains; currently 302 -> /campaign-temp. Recommendation: serve 301 with canonical to /webinar.

marco: Noted. I'll switch the rule to 301 for those hostnames and keep 302 for A/B variants. Will post PR.

jess: For internal linking: please enforce consistent anchor text: "Redwood Inference webinar" across /docs and /blog. We should run a quick anchor-text heatmap and patch the top 20 pages. Can someone run the export?

sam: I can run the export from Screaming Frog and filter by anchor text. Expect CSV by EOD.

alex: Great. Also: messaging iteration — benchmark narrative should call out baseline latency/cost numbers and how the webinar example shows a 20% cost reduction with prefix caching. Want that in the launch post.

marco: I'll add a comment in the PR with a short snippet for the launch post: "Benchmark: 25k concurrent tokens, p95 latency 220ms, cost/unit -20% vs baseline." Keep it editable.

jess: One more ops ask: inbound lead routing. When the landing form fires, make sure UTM+referrer are preserved across redirect chain. If we lose utm_source we lose attribution. Add server side append before redirect.

alex: Good call. Add to checklist: test form submission flow through the redirect chain and validate lead source in CRM.

sam: I'll add automated test case in Playwright for the flow: open landing -> simulate redirect variant -> submit form -> assert CRM payload contains utm_source.

marco: PR link when ready: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/web/compare/behavioral-redirects>

jess: Thanks everyone. Owner list: alex (product), marco (eng), sam (SEO/analytics). Follow-ups: attach ScreamingFrog CSV, PR link, and final redirect mapping before publish. :white_check_mark:
